name: Keeping customers separate
summary: Each customer's data belongs to their own organisation, and one customer can never read another's.

provenance.source: SimpleHire — its workspace-scoping model and the strict tenant-isolation guard that fails a query rather than letting it run unscoped
provenance.changes: Generalised from workspaces to organisations and reshaped for Next.js. The part kept deliberately intact is the refusal: an unscoped query throws instead of returning everybody's rows.

extensionPoints.description: Your own pages. Call requireOrg() at the top of anything that reads customer data.

postInstall: Every table that holds customer data needs an organizationId column. Ask the agent to add one when it creates a table.
limitations: Separation is enforced in the application, not by the database. A query written without scopedWhere() can still read across organisations — which is why the guard exists and why the tests check it.
solves: each customer only sees their own data
